name: Regular Grid
definition: A spatial acceleration structure that divides an Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) of a model into equal-sized voxels (cells). It reduces ray-primitive intersection tests by only checking primitives stored in voxels intersected by the ray.
summary: A Regular Grid is a spatial acceleration structure that divides a scene into a uniform 3D grid of cells to accelerate ray tracing by skipping empty space, unlike hierarchical structures that partition primitives into disjoint sets.
